White and the White House has signed an order that temporarily halts new sanctions against Russia.
The move comes just days before the sanctions were to take effect.
NPR's Franco Ordonez reports.
The sanctions were part of a package of financial measures designed to put pressure on Russia
and named after the late Senator Lindsey Graham, who led the effort.
Trump, who signed the legislation last month, put a hold on the implementation,
arguing that the pause was in the national interest.

that the U.S. would be purchasing diesel fuel from Russia.
Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky criticized the decision,
charging that the U.S. is easing pressure on Russia,
just as Russia carries out massive attacks on Ukraine's energy sector.
Zelensky wrote on social media that the Graham-led sanctions would have helped enormously,
and that more pressure is needed on Russia instead of financial rewards.
Franco Ordonez, NPR News.
Thousands of no-kings protests were seen around the country yesterday,

Keely Armstrong is a Democrat who took part in a protest in Fort Myers, Florida.
I'm hoping to send the message that it's important to vote no matter what your political party is,
because if we don't get out and vote, we can't change what we don't like.
It's estimated millions of Americans took part in the protest yesterday,
in big cities and small towns alike.
Pope Leo spoke to crowds in St. Peter's Square today.
This was the pontiff's first public event since undergoing surgery for lung cancer
just five days ago.
He walked out of the hospital yesterday and spoke today in a firm, clear voice.
Surgeons removed the lower lobe of the Pope's right lung.
They say there's no medical reason why Leo should not be able to travel next month
on a planned trip to Latin America.
A group of European diplomats has been assaulted by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank.
The attack came just one day after settlers wounded a Washington Post photojournalist.
NPR's Daniel Estrin has more from Tel Aviv.
Masked Israeli settlers targeted a group, including the Consul General of Belgium,
as well as a French mayor, who said they hit him with metal bars.
The diplomats were visiting a Palestinian village of the West Bank
to support residents as they harvested olives, which settlers have been violently disrupting.
The Israeli military called the attack on the diplomats a severe act of violence.
This happened one day after a Washington Post photojournalist was wounded in a settler assault.
U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee called that an act of terror.
Israel has not announced arrests in either attack.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office struck a skeptical tone,
saying more evidence was needed about both events.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
You're listening to NPR.
Do teachers feel like they matter?
A news survey finds only one in three teachers say they do.
NPR's Joe Naki Mehta has the story.
When educators feel valued, they're less likely to burn out and leave the profession.
But a quarter of teachers say they're likely to leave their jobs within a year.
Among those who felt like they matter little or not at all at school,
half say they don't plan to stay in education.
All this is from a new survey from Gallup,
the Mattering Institute and the Walton Family Foundation, which is a financial supporter of NPR.
Eighty-five percent of teachers reported their sense of mattering
comes through working directly with students and helping them work through difficult situations.
The report says schools and families can take steps to make sure their teachers feel valued
by formalizing appreciation, like by making recognition a part of school routines.
Administrators can also have regular conversations around
helping school staff grow and develop their careers.
Jenaki Mehta, NPR News.
Eight states are suing the artificial intelligence giant OpenAI.
They say the company's popular chatbot violates consumer protection laws
because it hurts children and deceives adults.
Iowa is among the states suing. It says OpenAI's chatbot model, ChatGPT,
is giving dangerous medical advice, encouraging paranoia
and coaching people to hurt others or kill themselves.
OpenAI says it has built safety protections into ChatGPT.
The other states involved in the lawsuit include Arizona and Arkansas.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News in Washington.
